items.review_rationale: Reviewed well-order as a total order on S with a least element for every nonempty subset; kept totality separate from the well-ordering minimum property and did not confuse least and merely minimal elements.

references.phrase: underlying relation is a partial order

references.context: Partial order with any two elements comparable, beyond the weaker partial-order condition.
Subset containing at least one element, quantified over all such subsets of S.
An a in A that is below or equal to every x in A under the given total order.

references.phrase: well order not mere linear order
references.disposition: Additional every-nonempty-subset least-element property distinguishes well order from arbitrary total order.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed concrete kernel of additive group homomorphism as zero preimage, with subgroup structure and its canonical inclusion; not confused with a generic categorical equalizer.

references.context: Mapping of abelian groups preserving addition and hence zero and inverses.
Identity element of the additive abelian group B.
Subset of A comprising all a for which f(a) equals the zero element of B.
Subset ker(f) of group A closed under group addition and inverses.

references.phrase: canonical subgroup inclusion ker(f) to A
references.context: Natural inclusion homomorphism sending each kernel element to the same element in A.

references.disposition: This specializes the abstract kernel universal-property notion to a concrete additive group.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed complex and exact sequence as composable arrows with consecutive zero composites, using image and kernel subobjects at every applicable position of an abelian category.

references.context: Chain of objects and morphisms with matching domains/codomains.
Composite of adjacent arrows equals distinguished zero morphism.

references.phrase: image subobject of X to Y
references.context: Categorical image of a morphism, represented by a subobject of its codomain; not simply the point-set image of a function.

references.phrase: equality im(X to Y)=ker(Y to Z)
references.context: Exactness at Y as equality of the corresponding subobjects, or their canonical equivalence in the abelian category.

references.phrase: zero object in short exact sequence
references.context: Distinguished zero object in the abelian category, supplying the endpoints 0→A→B→C→0.

references.disposition: The short exact form includes endpoint conditions and zero composites; the condition is not merely a complex.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed cokernel universal property for a morphism in a preadditive category, requiring p f=0 and unique factorization of any other arrow annihilating f; existence conditional.

references.phrase: zero morphism and equation p composed with f equals zero
references.context: The additive identity arrow in an abelian hom-set; p annihilates f under composition.
Any morphism q:Y to Z annihilating f uniquely factors as h composed with p, for one h:C to Z.
There is exactly one arrow from cokernel object C to Z satisfying q=h composed with p.

references.disposition: A general preadditive category need not supply a cokernel of every morphism; the definition is conditional on an exhibiting universal arrow.
